output.myth: Before a child learns the wind, the child gets a square kite with no tail. Ennu cut it from a sail too old to hold a boat, and gave it two sticks and a bridle of sinew. The tail is for steadiness, and a child is not steady yet, so the kite does without. Aun flew one like it the day before he cut the string, and that is why he was so sure the sky would hold. It did not. Now the first kite of every house hangs loose in the Spindle, and Hesk counts it each night. When a child lets go of the string for the first time, the old people say, the kite goes up a little way and comes back down into the hand. That is the only way anyone has found to fly back, and it is slow.
